articles.title: The best face oils for acne, dryness and more, according to dermatologists
articles.summary: Shop dermatologist-recommended face oils to hydrate the skin. Browse the best face oils for dry skin from Youth to the People, Herbivore and more.
articles.body: “Face oils are tricky,” says Kiran Mian, D.O, a board-certified dermatologist at Hudson Dermatology and Laser Surgery in New York City. One size rarely fits all in skin care and face oils are particularly nuanced. At their most basic, face oils are hydrators with both emollient and occlusive properties (meaning they help repair the skin barrier and lock in moisture), says Hadley King, M.D., board-certified dermatologist in New York City. But they can do so much more than moisturize. “Face oils definitely have a place with all different types of skin because they have a lot of different benefits,” says Navin Arora, M.D., a board-certified dermatologist and founder of Borealis Dermatology in New York, including treating acne and redness. Anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties can also deliver an added boost to your skin care routine. So, how do you find the right face oil for your skin type? Below, I rounded up everything you need to know when shopping for one and compiled a list of options to shop based on expert guidance. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. The best face oils I asked board-certified dermatologists for their favorite face oils for various skin types and concerns. Best overall In Arora’s opinion, the best face oils are those that come with antioxidant benefits as well as hydrating benefits. He likes Youth to the People’s Superberry Hydrate and Glow Face Dream Oil for its antioxidant-rich ingredient list, which has vitamins C and E and green tea to reduce inflammation. “Inflammation can come from a variety of things, either internal like rosacea or acne, or external like certain products, makeup or environmental exposures such as pollution and dust, which can cause the skin to flare up,” says Arora. “I think this face oil is really good at protecting you from the daily damage that’s done to your face.” Best for dry skin NBC Selected senior editor Nikki Brown says this oil from Herbivore is one of her favorite face oils to use during winter, especially after running or swimming. It treats redness and dry skin using blue tansy oil and squalane, according to the brand. “It has a clarifying effect on my skin without drying it out,” she says. “If I’m dealing with a teeny breakout, I’ll apply this before bed and when I wake up in the morning, the blemish is usually smaller and my skin looks generally better.” Best for sensitive skin For sensitive skin, King likes Ghost Democracy’s Softglow Facial Oil, which is rich in vitamin E, antioxidants and fatty acids — a combination she says helps repair cellular damage. It also has squalane that acts as both an emollient and occlusive, which means it is hydrating, too. It’s also free of mineral oil, essential oils, and fragrances, none of which are fundamentally bad, but can be irritating for certain skin types. Best for acne Mian’s favorite face oil is Herbivore’s Phoenix Rosehip Anti-Aging Face Oil. “It’s especially good for those with acne-prone skin,” she says. The fatty acids found in this oil mimic the natural skin barrier, which can help hydrate, says Arora. It also has antioxidant properties to help repair cell damage, according to the brand. But the most exciting benefit, particularly for those with acne, are the anti-inflammatory properties of rosehip oil, which make it ideal for treating pimples and other inflammatory skin conditions like rosacea and eczema. Best for full body Bio-Oil has long been favored by dermatologists for its ability to reduce the appearance of scars and stretch marks, and Arora often recommends it as a face oil. The mineral oil-based product includes vitamin E (a protective antioxidant), and chamomile, lavender, and rosemary oils, all of which have anti-inflammatory properties. For this reason, Arora likes Bio-Oil for those dealing with not only acne scars, but also rosacea. However, Bio-Oil does have potential allergens, including citronellol, limonene, and linalool, so be sure to test it on a small area of skin before applying it everywhere. Best vegan For a luxe option, King recommends Carter + Jane The Everything Oil. It’s pricey, but it has a bundle of oils in it, which work together to hydrate the skin and deliver antioxidant and anti-inflammatory benefits, according to King. She likes that it’s formulated without alcohol, making it less likely to be irritating to sensitive skin. It’s also vegan and cruelty-free, according to the brand. How I picked the best face oils Finding the optimal face oil for you starts with identifying your skin type and the issue you want to target, such as redness or acne. There’s also likely to be some trial and error involved, says Mian. There are, however, some general guidelines to keep in mind when vetting oils, according to our experts. Here’s what I kept in mind for our list: Skin barrier supporting ingredients. Certain face oils can mimic the natural skin barrier, helping strengthen the skin and resolve issues like dryness and redness, says Arora. Look for formulas with essential fatty acids and ceramides, both of which are emollients that can help repair damage. Antioxidant boosters. Many botanical oils, like jojoba and rosehip oil, are naturally rich in antioxidants and have anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial properties, says King. Other formulas have added antioxidants, like vitamin C, which can help repair cell damage and brighten skin. In fact, face oils can be the ideal delivery vehicle for active ingredients since they penetrate skin so well, says Arora. Comedogenic rating. “Some oils are more prone to clog your pores than others,” says Mian. Especially if you have acne-prone skin, it’s important to choose an oil with a low comedogenic rating (it runs on a scale of 0 to 5), meaning it is less likely to block pores. Low comedogenic oils include: grape seed oil (1), jojoba oil (2), hemp seed oil (0) and rosehip oil (1). “Sesame seed oil, flaxseed oil, almond oil, coconut oil and avocado oil are more prone to cause a blockage so I would have my acne patients avoid those,” says Mian. How to shop for face oil Want to know if a particular face oil is right for you? Keep these expert guidelines in mind before you buy: First and foremost, know your skin type Those with normal skin who are not sensitive and not prone to irritation or allergic reactions can most likely tolerate a variety of face oils and be fine, says Mian. If you’re acne-prone or deal with other inflammatory skin issues like rosacea, you can still benefit from face oils — you may just have to read ingredient lists a little more closely, she says. “Even then it may require some trial and error because it’s so individualized in terms of which oils are going to end up causing inflammation on your skin,” Mian says. When in doubt, consult your dermatologist. Understand comedogenic ratings If you’re acne prone, choosing an oil that is less likely to block your pores is particularly important, says Mian. “The rating is from zero to five, zero being less likely to clog your pores, five being very likely,” she explains. Jojoba, hemp seed and rosehip oil all have low comedogenic ratings while heavier oils include sesame seed oil, flaxseed oil, almond oil, coconut oil and avocado oil. Minimize the potential for irritation Certain ingredients found in face oils — including many essential oils — have the potential to irritate, says King. If you’re sensitive, she recommends avoiding formulas that have lime seed oil, lemon peel oil, limonene, linalool and citronellol since they can increase skin sensitivity. articles.title: How to clean stainless steel appliances: Expert tips and products to keep them shiny and streak-free
articles.summary: I learned the best way to clean stainless steel appliances, including the expert-recommend tools to use, like microfiber cloths and stainless steel wipes.
articles.body: The shiny, glossy appearance of stainless steel appliances can instantly elevate your kitchen’s appearance. What’s less appealing about stainless steel, however, is that it gets dirty very easily, with smudges, scratches, fingerprints and more. If you don’t have the right cleaning tools, it may feel like the best way to keep stainless steel appliances clean is to simply not use them. Fortunately — since avoiding your fridge and stove every day is not an option — there are a few easy ways to clean your stainless steel appliances while feeling confident about using them. I spoke with multiple cleaning experts to learn the best stainless steel cleaning methods, including the best (and worst) products to use on them. I also asked them to recommend products they love and use themselves. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. The best products for cleaning stainless appliances All of the products below are recommendations from our experts and have at least a four-star average rating from 500 reviews or more on Amazon. Weiman’s stainless steel cleaning products come recommended by both Kadi Dulude, owner of the cleaning company Wizard of Homes, and Robin Murphy, the chief cleaning officer at cleaning services company Maid Brigade. Both Dulude and Murphy say that Weiman’s stainless steel cleaning sprays and wipes are effective at getting rid of smudges and fingerprints. This bundle includes two bottles of wipes and a microfiber cloth that you can use to add shine to your appliances and buff small streaks. NBC Selected senior editor Shalwah Evans uses this on her dishwasher, oven, and microwave at least once a month. “I like that I can wipe down the appliances with these wipes and they stay pretty clean for weeks,” she says. “When paired with a microfiber cloth they keep my stainless steel sparkling and company ready.” In addition to the wipes and microfiber cloths, Weiman makes a stainless steel cleaning spray. It’s suitable for fridges, trash bins, ovens, dishwashers and more and it comes with a microfiber cloth. Shoppers say that the spray makes their appliances appear brand new and doesn’t leave streaks. And according to Murphy, it leaves a protective layer that prevents smudges and other residue from showing up later on. For cleaning your stainless steel appliances with simple dish soap, Murphy recommends using something eco-friendly, like Seventh Generation soap, which is plant based and free of fragrances. Eco-friendly ingredients tend to have less harsh ingredients that won’t wear on the surface of stainless steel appliances over time as much as non eco-friendly options, according to Murphy. Though not necessarily designed for cleaning stainless steel, it’s “safe, biodegradable, and effective at cutting grease without residue,” says Murphy. So it gets the job done. Plus, it’s “gentle enough for daily wipe-downs.” Add a few drops of this to a bowl with warm water before wiping with a microfiber cloth. Dawn’s Platinum Plus Powerwash Dish Spray may be one of the best cleaning products I’ve ever used. It’s incredibly versatile and, besides being great for cleaning dishes, it’s also suitable for occasional cleaning of grease from stainless steel. In my experience, it doesn’t leave streaks and it gets rid of smudges. I’ve also used it to clean the outside and inside of my fridge. It sprays in a foam texture and it has a refillable bottle — plus it’s available in a fragrance-free option. Microfiber cloths are ideal for many types of cleaning tasks, especially cleaning stainless steel, since they aren’t too rough or textured and won’t damage the surface of your appliances, according to Dulude. It’s also a good idea to have multiple microfiber cloths for cleaning different areas and for washing versus drying. If you prefer using a spray rather than wipes that already have a cleaning solution, you can try this option from Zep. It’s safe on your stainless steel appliances, including outdoor appliances like a grill. All you have to do is spray it onto the surface and then wipe with a microfiber cloth. This lavender-based stainless steel cleaner from Therapy is ideal if you want a cleaner with a pleasant smell. It includes a microfiber cloth that you use with the spray, which helps make your stainless steel fridge and dishwasher more resistant to fingerprints and streaks, according to the brand. How to clean stainless steel appliances in 4 easy steps or less There are a few methods and products that are ideal for cleaning stainless steel appliances. Here is what our experts recommend for a quick and simple clean: Get a new microfiber cloth, bowl with warm water and your favorite dish soap, such as Seventh Generation or Dawn Powerwash Dish Spray. Add a few drops of the dish soap to the bowl of warm water and mix it together.Fold the microfiber cloth a few times and then dunk it gently into the bowl of soapy warm water. Squeeze out any excess water.Use the cloth to wipe and buffer the surface of your stainless steel fridge, microwave, dishwasher or gas stovetop going with the grain. Dampen a second microfiber cloth with warm water and go over the stainless steel appliance once more. Then use a dry microfiber cloth to get rid of any water or residue. Alternatively, for a thorough clean, you can use stainless steel wipes, like Weiman Stainless Steel Cleaner and Polish Wipes, to wipe the surface of the stainless steel appliance, going with the grain. Then, use the dry microfiber cloth to wipe over the same area until it’s dry and shiny. What should you not use to clean stainless steel? Both Dulude and Murphy say that the most important thing when cleaning stainless steel is to avoid using abrasive ingredients and paper towels. This includes bleach, scouring pads or steel wool and oily products, according to Murphy. Similarly, you should avoid using scrub pads that are too abrasive and can leave scratches on the surface of stainless steel, according to Dulude. articles.title: Estatal italiana Poste Italiane passa a controlar indiretamente a TIM Brasil | G1
articles.standfirst: Empresa de correios da Itália ampliou sua participação na Telecom Italia, controladora direta da operadora brasileira, para 66,6%, em uma oferta avaliada em € 13 bilhões (R$ 76,82 bilhões).
articles.summary: Empresa de correios da Itália ampliou sua participação na Telecom Italia, controladora direta da operadora brasileira, para 66,6%, em uma oferta avaliada em € 13 bilhões (R$ 76,82 bilhões).
articles.body:
A TIM anunciou na sexta-feira (18) que a estatal italiana de correios Poste Italiane passou a ser a controladora indireta da operadora brasileira.

A mudança ocorreu após a empresa ampliar sua participação na Telecom Italia, controladora direta da TIM Brasil.

A Poste Italiane já detinha 20% da Telecom Italia e, na semana passada, assegurou uma participação de 66,6% na companhia por meio de uma oferta pelas ações, avaliada em cerca de 13 bilhões de euros (R$ 76,82 bilhões) .

“Em decorrência dessa aquisição originária de controle por meio de oferta pública, a Poste Italiane tornou-se a acionista controladora da TI e, consequentemente, a acionista controladora indireta da TIM Brasil”, disse a TIM em comunicado.

A Poste Italiane informou ainda que o período de adesão à oferta será reaberto de 21 a 25 de setembro de 2026, nos termos da regulamentação aplicável.

articles.title: Idosa fica ferida após parte de prédio desabar em Salvador  | G1
articles.standfirst: Acidente aconteceu no bairro da Ribeira. Proprietária foi notificada pela Codesal para corrigir dano estrutural. Vítima foi socorrida e levada para unidade de saúde.
articles.summary: Acidente aconteceu no bairro da Ribeira. Proprietária foi notificada pela Codesal para corrigir dano estrutural. Vítima foi socorrida e levada para unidade de saúde
articles.body:
A locatária de um imóvel ficou ferida após a varanda de um prédio de três andares desabar, na noite de domingo (20), no bairro da Ribeira, em Salvador .

Segundo apurou a TV Bahia, a vítima tem 86 anos e foi encaminhada para uma unidade de saúde depois do acidente. No entanto, não há detalhes sobre o estado dela.

Após vistoria, a Defesa Civil (Codesal) identificou um dano estrutural no imóvel. Em nota, o órgão informou que a proprietária do prédio será notificada para contratar um profissional habilitado para executar os reparos necessários.

Também foi encaminhada para a Secretaria Municipal de Desenvolvimento e Urbanismo (Sedur) uma solicitação para demolir as partes instáveis da estrutura.

Idosa fica ferida após parte de prédio desabar em Salvador — Foto: Reprodução/TV Bahia

A Codesal não pontuou se o local foi interditado. O g1 tentou, mas não tinha conseguido contato com a dona do prédio até a última atualização desta reportagem.

"A Defesa Civil de Salvador (Codesal) informa que neste domingo foi acionada pelo 199 e por isso uma equipe técnica esteve no local do desabamento parcial, em um imóvel residencial de três andares na Ribeira, para realizar vistoria.

Durante a vistoria, foi identificado dano estrutural parcial na varanda do imóvel.

Diante do risco, a proprietária, que apesar de não estar presente no momento da vistoria, já está ciente e será notificada para contratar um profissional habilitado, com registro no Conselho Regional de Engenharia e Agronomia (Crea) ou no Conselho Regional de Arquitetura e Urbanismo (Crau), para executar os reparos necessários. Também foi encaminhada ao órgão responsável a solicitação da demolição das partes instáveis e remanescentes da estrutura.

A Codesal reforça que não houve vítimas fatais. Uma senhora que é locatária do imóvel ficou ferida e foi prontamente atendida e encaminhada para um hospital da cidade.

Por fim, a orientação é de que em caso de emergência, a população se mantenha afastada do risco, vá para um local seguro imediatamente, acione a Codesal pelo telefone 199, disponível 24 horas por dia, todos os dias da semana, inclusive aos feriados, e de que também realize o cadastro gratuito do CEP, via SMS, por meio do número 40199".

articles.title: Engenharia ganha espaço no Agreste com avanço da indústria e da construção civil | G1
articles.standfirst: Expansão de projetos de infraestrutura, habitação e produção amplia a demanda por profissionais preparados para inovação, tecnologia e sustentabilidade
articles.summary: Expansão de projetos de infraestrutura, habitação e produção amplia a demanda por profissionais preparados para inovação, tecnologia e sustentabilidade
articles.body:
O crescimento do polo industrial e do setor da construção civil no Agreste de Pernambuco vem aumentando também a necessidade de profissionais qualificados para acompanhar as transformações da região. Em cidades como Caruaru, que funciona como um dos principais polos econômicos do interior, engenheiros e arquitetos ganham espaço em projetos ligados à infraestrutura, produção, habitação e desenvolvimento urbano.

O movimento também coloca as instituições de ensino superior diante de um desafio: preparar profissionais capazes de atender às novas demandas do mercado sem deixar de lado questões como sustentabilidade, inovação e uso eficiente dos recursos.

A Asces-Unita, uma das instituições de ensino superior mais conceituadas de Caruaru, oferta os cursos de Engenharia Ambiental, Civil, Produção e Química. Segundo Jeferson Mendonça, coordenador dos cursos, a área é estritamente ligada à tecnologia e à inovação.

Para desenvolver os cursos com excelência, a instituição acompanha todas as evoluções do mercado e já utiliza mecanismos para preparar os alunos para as novas demandas do mercado.

“A formação de profissionais nessa área das engenharias, de maneira geral, é fundamental. São esses profissionais, com competência técnica, que vão ajudar essas organizações a gerenciar processos, desenvolver pessoas, aplicar ferramentas inovadoras. São esses profissionais com habilidades técnicas que vão fazer com que as empresas consigam dar saltos e fazer toda a diferença”, destaca o coordenador, Jeferson Mendonça.

Indo além do crescimento e pensando também nas demandas sustentáveis, cada vez mais presentes no mercado, há uma aliança no curso de Engenharia Civil com a Engenharia Ambiental. O curso realiza um projeto integrador em que as duas áreas atuam juntas para o desenvolvimento de projetos sustentáveis.

“Dentro da Engenharia Civil, no ano passado, nós desenvolvemos, em parceria com a construtora AWA, um projeto de iniciação científica voltado para gestão de resíduos sólidos e práticas ESG dentro da construção civil. Além disso, dentro desse eixo de sustentabilidade, há a possibilidade de esses alunos atuarem em parceria com empresas num projeto de extensão voltado especificamente para a redução desses desperdícios utilizando a inteligência artificial”, conta Jeferson.

Contato com situações reais de campo faz parte da formação dos estudantes, fortalecendo a integração entre conhecimento acadêmico e prática profissional. — Foto: Asces-Unita/Divulgação

Diferenciais como os citados pelo coordenador do curso atraem estudantes de diversas regiões de Pernambuco. Uma delas foi Letícia Mendes, aluna de Engenharia Civil. A jovem veio de Cumaru, no Agreste do Estado. A escolha pela Asces veio pela reputação da instituição, construída ao longo dos anos.

“Minha certeza veio quando participei do evento 'Asces Portas Abertas' no ensino médio; ao conhecer a estrutura, me visualizei estudando ali. Hoje, como aluna de Engenharia Civil, vejo que minhas expectativas foram totalmente superadas e tenho a convicção de que estou construindo uma base sólida para minha carreira”, disse Letícia.

Estrutura da Asces-Unita em Caruaru, instituição que oferece cursos de Engenharia Ambiental, Civil, de Produção e Química. — Foto: Asces-Unita/Divulgação

Uma das alunas que faz parte do curso de Engenharia Civil é Alessandra França, que está no quinto período da graduação. Atualmente, ela faz estágio em um escritório de projetos estruturais, hidrossanitários e elétricos. Dentro da Asces, ela também participa de um projeto de extensão voltado para o meio ambiente.

Estudantes acompanham projetos e atividades práticas, desenvolvendo conhecimentos que podem ser aplicados às diferentes áreas das Engenharias. — Foto: Asces-Unita/Divulgação

“Sempre procuro ficar atualizada com as novidades na área. Estou envolvida em um projeto sobre clima e sustentabilidade. Sempre tento relacionar os conteúdos de sala à prática, ver como tudo funciona e como surgem obstáculos durante a execução das atividades”, disse Alessandra.

Aliando novas tendências e diferenciais, a Asces se destaca também por promover eventos em que os alunos têm contato com profissionais atuantes no mercado, o que permite a compreensão das novas tecnologias e transformações em todas as áreas das Engenharias.

Atividades práticas aproximam os estudantes da realidade profissional e contribuem para uma formação conectada aos desafios da Engenharia e da construção civil. — Foto: Asces-Unita/Divulgação

articles.summary: Danielle encontrou no empreendedorismo cooperativo um caminho para crescer como professora e gestora
articles.body:
DANIELLE COMEÇOU COMO PROFESSORA NA COOPERATIVA DE TRABALHO EDUCACIONAL COLÉGIO PROFESSOR CLÓVIS TAVARES. — Foto: ANDERSON PIRES

Em uma cooperativa educacional, quem ensina também pode ser dono da escola. Professores se unem para empreender, participar das decisões e construir juntos os caminhos do negócio. É uma relação diferente com o trabalho: a escola também é sua, o resultado depende de todos e cada decisão tem impacto direto na educação dos alunos.

As cooperativas educacionais podem ser formadas por professores ou até por pais de alunos. Quando os educadores são os cooperados, como acontece na cooperativa Pró-Uni, em Campos dos Goytacazes, eles assumem dois papéis: são profissionais da educação e donos do próprio negócio. Participam da gestão, dividem responsabilidades e trabalham pelo crescimento de um patrimônio construído coletivamente.

Esse modelo também faz diferença na formação dos alunos. Eles aprendem a importância da cooperação, do respeito e da responsabilidade, mas vão além: convivem com uma escola em que pessoas se unem para empreender, tomar decisões e construir resultados coletivamente. Na prática, conhecem desde cedo uma forma de fazer negócio em que ninguém cresce sozinho e o desenvolvimento é compartilhado.

Foi nesse ambiente que Danielle Barros Duarte construiu boa parte de sua vida profissional. Graduada em História e Ciências Sociais, ela chegou à Pró-Uni há mais de duas décadas como professora. Depois, passou pela coordenação pedagógica e pelo conselho fiscal até chegar à diretoria e à presidência da cooperativa.

“Eu escolhi ensinar ‘história’, mas foi a cooperação que escreveu os melhores capítulos do meu próprio enredo. Trabalhava em uma faculdade, mas, após o nascimento das minhas filhas, busquei novas possibilidades de atuação que me permitissem conciliar a carreira com a maternidade. Desde então, concentrei minhas atividades no cooperativismo, que considero meu porto seguro” , contou.

A trajetória de Danielle mostra uma característica própria desse modelo de negócio. Na Pró-Uni, o professor não é apenas responsável por ensinar. Como cooperado, é também um dos donos da escola. Participa das decisões, assume responsabilidades sobre o negócio e trabalha pelo crescimento de algo que também é seu. Uma relação que aumenta o sentimento de pertencimento e aproxima ainda mais o educador do futuro da escola e de seus alunos.

HOJE DANIELLE ATUA NA DIREÇÃO E PRESIDÊNCIA DA COOPERATIVA PRÓ-UNI. — Foto: ANDERSON PIRES

Para Danielle, o cooperativismo também abriu portas para o desenvolvimento profissional. Ao longo de sua trajetória, encontrou oportunidades de capacitação e ampliou sua atuação dentro e fora da escola. No ano passado, participou de uma missão internacional de capacitação na Espanha e, em setembro deste ano, se prepara para conhecer a China.

“Oportunidades que não são encontradas em qualquer lugar. Hoje, exerço atividades administrativas, sem deixar de lado a sala de aula, conciliando, de forma mais leve, os papéis de educadora, gestora e mãe. Por ter minhas filhas, de 12 e 9 anos, matriculadas na cooperativa educacional, consigo perceber em casa os reflexos das decisões tomadas durante minha gestão. Me sinto realizada em cooperar com a sociedade” , concluiu.

Na história de Danielle, os diferentes papéis se encontram no mesmo lugar. Ela é professora, cooperada, gestora, presidente e mãe de duas alunas da escola. Ensina, participa das decisões e acompanha, dentro de casa, o resultado do trabalho realizado todos os dias. Uma trajetória que mostra como o cooperativismo pode transformar uma profissão em oportunidade para empreender, crescer e participar diretamente da construção do negócio.

E esse aprendizado não fica restrito aos professores. Ao conviverem com uma escola organizada de forma cooperativa, os alunos descobrem que empreender também pode significar unir pessoas, compartilhar decisões e construir resultados que beneficiem o grupo. Uma experiência que leva o cooperativismo para além da sala de aula e ajuda a formar uma nova geração que conhece, desde cedo, o valor do empreendedorismo coletivo.

Para o presidente do Sistema OCB/RJ, Vinicius Mesquita, uma escola cooperativa também apresenta aos jovens uma forma diferente de enxergar o futuro profissional e o empreendedorismo.

“Quando falamos em preparar um jovem para o futuro, também precisamos mostrar que existem diferentes caminhos para empreender. Em uma escola cooperativa, o aluno convive com um negócio que nasceu da união de pessoas e percebe, na prática, que é possível transformar conhecimento em trabalho, renda e oportunidade de forma coletiva. Talvez amanhã esse jovem queira abrir uma empresa, exercer uma profissão ou criar uma cooperativa. O importante é que ele saia da escola sabendo que empreender junto também é uma escolha” , destaca Vinicius.

A história de Danielle e sua relação com o Pró-Uni fazem parte do Momento SomosCoop , série produzida pelo Sistema OCB/RJ para mostrar, por meio de histórias reais, como o cooperativismo transforma trajetórias, fortalece negócios e gera desenvolvimento nas comunidades onde está presente.

O SomosCoop é o movimento nacional de valorização do cooperativismo. A iniciativa conecta cooperativas, cooperados e a sociedade em torno de um propósito: tornar o Coop cada vez mais conhecido e reconhecido e mostrar os impactos positivos desse modelo de negócio para quem produz, trabalha, empreende e consome.

O movimento também convida o consumidor a fazer parte desse ciclo. Ao escolher produtos e serviços de cooperativas, ele contribui para a geração de trabalho, renda e desenvolvimento local. O carimbo SomosCoop ajuda a identificar produtos e serviços cooperativistas e torna essa escolha mais simples no dia a dia. Detalhes sobre o cooperativismo e seu avanço, são encontrados no site

articles.title: Criança se emociona ao receber visita surpresa de policiais em festa | G1
articles.standfirst: Davi Luís comemorou o aniversário de cinco anos com o tema da Companhia de Policiamento Especializado (CPE) da Polícia Militar de Goiás. Festa aconteceu na última quarta-feira (16).
articles.summary: Davi Luís comemorou o aniversário de cinco anos com o tema da Companhia de Policiamento Especializado (CPE) da Polícia Militar de Goiás.
articles.body:
O pequeno Davi Luís, de 5 anos, se emocionou ao receber uma visita surpresa de policiais da Companhia de Policiamento Especializado (CPE) da Polícia Militar de Goiás (PMGO) durante a sua festa de aniversário, em Anápolis , região central de Goiás. Fã da corporação, o menino escolheu a própria tropa especializada como tema da comemoração (assista acima) .

A festa foi realizada na última quarta-feira (16), segundo informou ao g1 o tenente Leonardo Borges. O militar informou que a surpresa foi combinada após a mãe do menino entrar em contato com o comando da CPE e pedir uma viatura no aniversário. Como havia uma equipe disponível na escala naquele momento, os militares foram autorizados a atender ao pedido e prestar a homenagem.

No vídeo, Davi aparece com uma farda semelhante à da corporação . A temática militar também marcou presença nos detalhes da decoração, nos doces e no bolo com as cores e insígnias da tropa. A mãe do menino, Natalia Garcia, relatou que a festa foi realizada em casa e restrita a familiares e amigos próximos, mas a visita dos policiais superou qualquer expectativa e marcou profundamente o filho.

"A gente não imaginou que teria essa proporção toda, mas ele ficou muito feliz. Era uma coisa simples, só entre família mesmo e amigos próximos aqui na nossa casa, e receber eles assim... ele ficou radiante. Foi dormir falando desse momento", destacou Natalia.

Criança se emociona ao receber visita surpresa de policiais em aniversário; vídeo — Foto: Arquivo pessoal/Jorge Lu

O menino também presta continência para os policiais e posa para fotos. A equipe que esteve na residência contava com quatro policiais militares, incluindo o sargento Urbano e o cabo Reis.

"Os policiais foram lá, deram um abraço nele e tiraram as fotos ao lado do bolo e na viatura. Foi uma forma de incentivar e de manter esse contato próximo", explicou o militar.

Durante a visita, os agentes abraçaram o garoto, posaram para fotografias ao lado do aniversariante na mesa do bolo e junto à viatura operacional. Em nota, a CPE de Anápolis informou que a presença dos militares buscou tornar a data especial para Davi e sua família.

articles.title: Moroccan parties mobilise in markets and online for parliamentary elections
articles.summary: Moroccan parties are pushing campaigns before the September 23 vote to secure 395 parliamentary seats.
articles.body:
Political parties in Morocco are intensifying campaign efforts before legislative elections on September 23, which will ultimately decide Morocco’s next government.

Twenty-seven political parties are competing for 395 seats in the House of Representatives and the vote comes at a crucial time for the country.

Rising living costs, pressure on public services, and high youth unemployment – currently at 37.3 percent for Moroccans aged 15 to 24 – are all issues being hotly debated.

Party headquarters across Morocco and sites at packed city neighbourhoods and markets have been transformed into electioneering operation rooms. Campaign teams navigate crowded streets with loudspeakers, music, and leaflets to catch the attention of Morocco’s 15.8 million registered voters.

“We choose communication locations carefully; we start from a field map where we define the spaces where citizens meet naturally, then we divide the team according to tasks between direct communication and recording observations,” al-Wali al-Shtouki, campaign manager for the Justice and Development Party (PJD) in the Medina-Sidi Youssef Ben Ali district, told Al Jazeera.

“We also hold small meetings at the headquarters because they allow a calm and direct dialogue to understand what the citizen actually expects. What we hear in the field is what guides our daily work. After every tour or meeting, we collect observations and repeated questions and discuss them within the team, then we distinguish between local issues that need follow-up and those related to public policies and parliamentary work.”

While physical headquarters serve as hubs for election campaigns, a party’s success ultimately relies on its roots within a community, Jawad al-Shafdi, head of the Moroccan Observatory for Political Participation, said.

“In the Moroccan case, the strength of the candidate, their local extension, their network of relationships, and their electoral record also play essential roles,” al-Shafdi told Al Jazeera.

“We may find a party with limited organisational presence in a specific district achieving a significant result thanks to a strong candidate, and vice versa. Winning votes is achieved through a more complex system that combines party organisation, candidate strength, local extension, networks of elected officials, direct and digital communication, in addition to the party’s image and political offering.

“Therefore, the true criterion is not the number of people who enter the headquarters, but its ability to convert organisational movement into electoral mobilisation, mobilisation into votes, and votes into seats.”

The competition has forced political groups to adopt multi-channel strategies that balance street-level outreach with digital campaigns to reach a broader audience.

Fatima al-Tamni, a candidate for the Left Alliance in the Ain Sebaa – Hay Mohammadi district in Casablanca, highlighted the necessity of direct engagement with voters rather than superficial campaign displays.

She believes that party campaigns should serve as a space to listen to the concerns of the electorate and propose solutions, while building a strategic vision for transport, housing, pollution and other issues.

“We do not want to speak to the citizen from above, nor turn the campaign into a festival of pictures and slogans… We want to speak with them in clear language, and hear from them before we speak in their name,” she said. “[It] is not an end in itself, but the beginning of a new political relationship with citizens based on clarity, accountability, and fulfilling commitments.”

Youssef Ait Sidi Said, a political activist with the Progress and Socialism Party in the Chichaoua province, said campaigning remains an evolving process.

“For the party, this campaign is no longer just a specific period to introduce candidates and the electoral programme, but has become an opportunity for direct and continuous communication with the population and listening to their concerns and expectations,” Ait Sidi Said told Al Jazeera.

“Digital platforms allow reaching broad groups, especially youth, and grant them the possibility to interact, ask questions, and express their opinions. However, we do not consider that digitisation can replace direct communication. On the contrary, we see that each tool has its function.”

Ultimately, direct engagement with voters should remain the hallmark of party campaigns, he said.

“Field communication allows direct listening to the citizen, while digital platforms allow expanding the reach, interaction, and documenting activities,” Ait Sidi Said added.

articles.title: US woman fatally shot by boyfriend 'playing' with gun days before engagement; he later shoots himself
articles.summary: US News: A 21-year-old woman was fatally shot by her boyfriend in Alaska while he was handling a revolver, before he later shot himself with another firearm, T.
articles.body: A 21-year-old woman was fatally shot by her boyfriend in Alaska while he was handling a revolver, before he later shot himself with another firearm, The New York Post reported.CloeRae McBrayer was killed by Landon Lowrance, 22, last Wednesday, just days before the couple had planned to get engaged, according to her family.The Fairbanks Police Department said Lowrance pointed the revolver at McBrayer while playing with it and fired. McBrayer was pronounced dead at the scene when officers arrived.911 call led police to sceneA friend of Lowrance's called 911 after the shooting and remained on the phone with dispatchers as police responded.Police said a disturbance could be heard in the background during the call. The friend then tried to intervene after Lowrance obtained another firearm and shot himself.Lowrance was found critically injured and taken to Fairbanks Memorial Hospital, where he later died.Police said the caller was questioned by detectives and is not believed to have been involved in either shooting. Authorities have not disclosed whose home the incident took place at.Family remembers woman who planned to become teacherMcBrayer was studying towards a career in teaching and had recently been accepted to the University of Alaska Fairbanks, according to her family.Her mother, Amanda Hooper, described her daughter as an outgoing and caring person who had been raised in Alabama."She's the sunshine of the family. She'd love to be the center of attention. She's bubbly, she wants you to talk to everybody. She would sing, she helped everybody," Hooper told Alaska's News Source.Hooper said McBrayer and Lowrance had met through a mutual friend and were planning to get engaged that weekend."I talked to his mom, she seems like a really good family, and they were talking about getting engaged this weekend and then all this," she said.McBrayer's older sister, Lori Hunt, told the outlet: "We were planning their wedding."Police urge firearm safetyFairbanks police described the deaths as a "tragic and preventable loss of life" and urged people to follow basic firearm safety practices."Firearms should always be handled responsibly and safely, and individuals should never participate in games or activities involving firearms that place anyone at risk of injury or death," the department said.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Flight disruption: Airlines criticise air traffic control over second glitch in a month
articles.summary: Airlines are angry about the delays, with EasyJet saying the latest incident "once again calls into question the resilience" of the system.
articles.body:
Airlines have criticised the UK's air traffic control system after a second technical problem in two weeks caused major disruption to UK flights

EasyJet said Monday's incident "once again calls into question the resilience" of how the service works, while Wizz Air said there was a "national confidence crisis" in National Air Traffic Services (Nats), which runs the UK's air traffic.

The technical problem at Prestwick caused disruption at airports across Scotland, Northern Ireland and northern England, with around 150 flights cancelled.

Nats said a "connectivity issue" was to blame for the disruption, and that it had "nothing to do" with a separate software defect at Swanwick that led to the cancellation of 2,000 flights earlier in September.

The underlying issue causing Monday's disruption has since been resolved, with Nats saying it was running at "full capacity" although officials warned of knock-on effects.

A spokesperson said they were now "focused on working with our customers to recover their residual delays and help get their operations back to normal".

Easyjet was the worst affected airline, with 47 of its 670 scheduled departures cancelled, while British Airways has seen 12 cancellations from its 513 scheduled departures.

The UK Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) said passengers who had flights disrupted were "unlikely" to be entitled to compensation.

It said the technical issue is "likely to be considered the result of 'extraordinary circumstances' under passenger rights rules", meaning that "although passengers should be looked after by airlines, they are unlikely to be entitled to compensation for delays or cancellations that were directly caused by the incident".

An independent review by the CAA into the resilience of the UK's air traffic control system is under way and the results will be published "within six months", it said.

Repeated air traffic control failures leave us in worrying territory

Flight chaos caused by 'millisecond' software defect, report says

UK flight delays continue after issue with air traffic control in Scotland is fixed

Industry representative body Airlines UK said both passengers and airlines "deserve better" service after "yet another Nats failure".

Managing director of Wizz Air UK, Yvonne Moynihan, called for "urgent reform" of Nats, adding that she did not have confidence in its current leadership.

Asked on BBC Radio 4's World at One programme if Nats chief Martin Rolfe should resign, Moynihan said: "We need to look at the leadership at the top. But more than that, what are the board of directors doing?"

Jet2 boss Steve Heapy called for "urgent and accountable" action to bolster the UK's air traffic control infrastructure.

Ryanair reiterated its calls for Rolfe to resign, saying he had failed to deliver" either a reliable system or an effective back-up". The latest outage affected 140 of the airline's flights and 25,000 passengers.

British Airways said "yet another technical fault with Nats" was "disappointing".

A Nats spokesperson apologised, saying: "In the real world, we accept technology can and sometimes does fail. Our job is minimising disruption where possible.

"What isn't acceptable is any incident where safety is compromised - this is always our first priority."

They added that it was working to return air traffic to normal as quickly as possible and urged passengers to check their flight status with their airline.

Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander acknowledged the situation was "deeply frustrating" for passengers.

Steve Davies, 74, told the BBC he was "cheesed off with air traffic control" as technical issues with its systems seemed to be "happening a lot".

He and his wife Sadie became stuck at Birmingham airport after being told to disembark their EasyJet flight to Edinburgh on Monday morning.

Nicole McCloskey, from Kilmarnock, had been due to go to Disneyland Paris with her family before their flight was cancelled.

She told the BBC her family got a message to say the flight was delayed while they were travelling to Glasgow airport, but only found out it had been grounded altogether once they arrived.

Nicole said they have been rebooked on another flight on later on Monday and were hopeful "it's sorted in time".

Rebecca Freeman became stranded at Bristol Airport after her flight to Edinburgh for a business meeting was cancelled. She described the atmosphere as "chaos".

"I was caught up in the Nats issue earlier this month and spent nine hours at Bristol airport," she told the BBC.

"I can't believe it's happened again. It is very frustrating and I will have to attempt the business meeting again for a third time," adding that she still has not received money back from the associated costs for the last time her flights were cancelled.

Not much is known about what caused the latest Nats problems, except that there was a technical failure at its control centre in Prestwick, which handles traffic across northern England, Scotland and Northern Ireland - catering for about 42% of the UK's air traffic.

The other Nats centre at Swanwick in Hampshire looks after airspace in the southern part of the UK, including the approaches to Heathrow and Gatwick.

Last month's Swanwick incident affected hundreds of thousands of passengers, with some sleeping on airport floors or getting stuck overseas earlier this month.

It was more severe as it affected intercontinental and long-haul travel via UK airspace.

Nats said in a report last week that the software glitch happened "in the space of a millisecond" leading to the system producing corrupted data.

Sources say that behind the scenes, airlines are "furious" that disruption keeps on happening, and that they must bear the costs of refunding passengers and looking after those affected by delays.

There are deep concerns that not enough resources are being put into ensuring the air traffic control system has the resilience it needs.

Rolfe told the BBC at the time of the Swanwick incident that he would not resign, saying the software defect was "very, very obscure".

articles.title: The 'rebel' hit by rebellion: How Mamata Banerjee's TMC journey has come full circle
articles.summary: India News: Mamata Banerjee's political journey in West Bengal has come almost full circle.In 1998, Mamata walked out of the Congress after years of differences w.
articles.body: Mamata Banerjee's political journey in West Bengal has come almost full circle.In 1998, Mamata walked out of the Congress after years of differences with its leadership and formed the Trinamool Congress. She believed the Congress was not doing enough to challenge the Left Front, which had been ruling West Bengal for decades.28 years later, Didi, as she is fondly called, is now herself a step away from losing control of her party to a rebellion. Her Trinamool Congress has split, and rivals in the party, who once worked under her are now challenging her control. The Election Commission has temporarily frozen the party's original name and its well-known 'Jora Ghash Phul' (flowers and grass) symbol while it decides which faction has the “real” claim.And what's more! In an interesting turn of events, Mamata is now desperately banking on the Congress’s support to survive the BJP’s political offensive against her in West Bengal.The change comes at a difficult moment for her.The BJP recently ended Trinamool’s 15-year rule in West Bengal in May, crossing 200 seats and forming its first government in the state. Mamata’s party, which had been in power for 15 years, fell below 100 seats.(function(){function e(){window.addEventListener(`message`,function(e){if(e.data[`datawrapper-height`]!==void 0){var t=document.querySelectorAll(`iframe`);for(var n in e.data[`datawrapper-height`])for(var r=0,i;i=t[r];r++)if(i.contentWindow===e.source){var a=e.data[`datawrapper-height`][n]+`px`;i.style.height=a}}})}e()})();Mamata's troubles have only grown since then.The defeat was followed by a rebellion within the TMC and finally a battle over who has the right to use the party’s name and symbol.For a leader who built her career as a rebel, Mamata is now facing a rebellion of her own.Congress: From bitter rival to 'sister party'At the peak of her power-packed 15 years as chief minister of West Bengal, Mamata refused to acknowledge the presence of Congress in West Bengal. In fact, for Mamata, both the Congress and the Left were bitter political rivals and she would often accuse them of being the B-team of the BJP in the state. But that changed in the aftermath of her crushing defeat in May this year as the BJP swept the state’s political landscape and formed its first government.The shift in power dynamics was on display when Mamata announced support for the Congress candidate in the Nandigram bypoll to be held on October 6. "We are extending our support to Congress in Nandigram. We are doing this for the greater interest of the nation,” Mamata Banerjee announced. But what really surprised was her reference to the Congress as a “natural alliance” and a “sister party”. Words that would sound almost alien to those who have followed Mamata’s politics, especially the Congress leaders in the state.While the Congress has strongly backed her fight against the Election Commission, with Rahul Gandhi leading the charge, the help is unlikely to transform into a greater alliance, at least for now. The West Bengal Congress unit, which was at the receiving end of Mamata’s political aggression for many years, is very clear and categorical that it does not want any alliance with her party.Vendetta politicsSince losing power, Mamata has repeatedly accused the BJP of targeting her and trying to weaken her party.The irony is that Mamata herself faced similar accusations after she came to power in 2011, ending 34 years of Left rule. Both the Left and the Congress had accused the Trinamool of using political pressure and defections to weaken its rivals.(function(){function e(){window.addEventListener(`message`,function(e){if(e.data[`datawrapper-height`]!==void 0){var t=document.querySelectorAll(`iframe`);for(var n in e.data[`datawrapper-height`])for(var r=0,i;i=t[r];r++)if(i.contentWindow===e.source){var a=e.data[`datawrapper-height`][n]+`px`;i.style.height=a}}})}e()})();The circumstances may be different, but the roles have now reversed. What is happening today to her is what she did to her opponents in the past in West Bengal.Mamata's beginning in politicsMamata started her political career with the Congress in the 1970s. The first glimpse of her aggressive political style was on display during Emergency days when she made headlines for her protest against Jay Prakash Narayan.She quickly rose through the Congress ranks and, in 1984, emerged as the giant killer when she defeated veteran Communist politician Somnath Chatterjee, to win the Jadavpur parliamentary Constituency in West Bengal. She was also among the youngest MPs elected that year.There has been no looking back since then. She lost in 1989, but came back strongly in 1991 from the Calcutta South constituency and retained the seat in 1996, 1998, 1999, 2004 and 2009 Lok Sabha elections.The protest politics and the birth of Trinamool CongressMamata's differences with the Congress grew through the 1990s. She believed the party was not aggressive enough in taking on the Left government in West Bengal.Her politics was built around street protests and agitations against the Left government.One of the most prominent moments of her political career came in 1993, as state Youth Congress chief, when she led a march to Writers’ Building demanding voter ID cards to prevent alleged electoral malpractice.Police opened fire during the protest, killing 13 Congress workers. By 1997, her differences with the Congress leadership had reached a breaking point. In 1998, Mamata walked out and formed the Trinamool Congress.Years later, the Singur and Nandigram movements turned that protest politics into a force strong enough to bring her to power for a good 15 years.Nandigram challenge, once againNandigram has always had a special place in Mamata's political career. The land protests here in 2007 helped turn her into the strongest challenger to the Left. Four years later, she came to power.But Nandigram also became one of her biggest electoral setbacks. In the 2021 assembly election, Mamata chose to contest from the seat against her former aide Suvendu Adhikari, who had joined the BJP. Nandigram was Suvendu’s bastion and Mamata wanted to prove a point. That did not happen as she lost to Suvendu by around 2,000 votes. But her Trinamool Congress returned to power in the state with a thumping majority.Five years later, in 2026, it was Suvendu’s turn to challenge Mamata in her bastion of Bhabanipur, while also contesting from Nandigram. Suvendu not just reinforced his dominance in Nandigram but also humiliated Mamata in Bhabanipur.Suvendu retained Bhabanipur and vacated Nandigram, necessitating a bypoll. But this time around Mamata faced a setback even before the contest could begin. Her candidate for the October 6 bypoll in Nandigram withdrew from the contest after meeting chief minister Suvendu Adhikari, leaving Mamata without a candidate of her own. She then announced support for Congress candidate Milan Pradhan.For Mamata, Nandigram has now seen almost every phase of her politics. It helped her rise, handed her a personal defeat, and is now showing the challenges she faces after losing power.(function(){function e(){window.addEventListener(`message`,function(e){if(e.data[`datawrapper-height`]!==void 0){var t=document.querySelectorAll(`iframe`);for(var n in e.data[`datawrapper-height`])for(var r=0,i;i=t[r];r++)if(i.contentWindow===e.source){var a=e.data[`datawrapper-height`][n]+`px`;i.style.height=a}}})}e()})();The road ahead ...For Mamata, the road ahead is not just about fighting the BJP. The former chief minister has a larger issue at hand at the moment. She has to hold her party together, fight for control of the Trinamool name and symbol, and rebuild her position as the main opposition force in Bengal.Congress support could help her on some issues, especially at the national level, but a wider alliance in Bengal seems unlikely, at least for now.Congress leaders in West Bengal remain wary of Mamata after years of on-and-off rivalry and large-scale defections from their party to the Trinamool under Mamata’s watch.That leaves Mamata at the junction of perhaps the most difficult phase of her political career.She began as a Congress leader, broke away in rebellion, built a party of her own and eventually ruled Bengal for 15 years. Now, with rebels challenging that very party and she being forced to return to Congress for help, Mamata's journey has indeed come almost full circle.The future and fate of the original Trinamool Congress is now in the hands of the Election Commission. Mamata will be keeping her fingers crossed. And rightly so. Precedents from recent past in Maharashtra would worry her. Sharad Pawar lost control of the Nationalist Congress Party and Uddhav Thackeray of Shiv Sena, after the ECI ruled in favour of rebels who had split the two parties. articles.title: New York leads US in Gen Z exodus as young adults seek cheaper housing
articles.summary: News News: New York recorded the biggest net outflow of Gen Z adults among US metropolitan areas in 2024, with 29,554 more young people leaving than moving in, a.
articles.body: New York recorded the biggest net outflow of Gen Z adults among US metropolitan areas in 2024, with 29,554 more young people leaving than moving in, according to a Redfin analysis of US Census Bureau data.The migration, however, does not necessarily mean young Americans are abandoning major cities altogether. Many are making relatively short moves to nearby metropolitan areas, allowing them to stay within reach of existing social and professional networks while seeking lower housing costs and job opportunities.One of the clearest examples is the New York-Philadelphia corridor.Some 9,284 Gen Z adults moved from the New York metropolitan area to Philadelphia in 2024, making it the second-most popular migration route for the generation.The move also comes with a significant difference in housing costs. The typical home in the New York metro sells for about $832,000, compared with around $309,000 in Philadelphia, according to Redfin.Los Angeles-Riverside tops Gen Z migration routesThe most popular Gen Z migration route in 2024 was from Los Angeles to Riverside, California, with 10,261 people making the roughly 60-mile move.New York to Philadelphia ranked second, followed by Los Angeles to San Diego, which attracted 9,237 Gen Z movers, according to the New York Post.San Antonio recorded the largest net gain of Gen Z movers, at 10,678, followed by Washington, DC, with 8,631; Austin, with 8,590; Nashville, with 8,093; and Dallas, with 6,944, Forbes reported.Texas accounted for three of the five biggest destinations, with San Antonio, Austin and Dallas recording a combined net inflow of 26,212 Gen Z adults in 2024.New York's net Gen Z outflow of 29,554 was followed by Minneapolis at 17,815, Los Angeles at 16,465, Denver at 13,882 and Detroit at 11,696.Millennials are moving for different reasonsNew York also recorded the largest net millennial outflow among US metropolitan areas, losing 42,698 millennials in 2024. Los Angeles followed with a net outflow of 31,107, while Miami lost 21,373, according to the Redfin analysis.The destinations favoured by millennials differed from those attracting Gen Z. Houston recorded the biggest net millennial inflow at 16,365, followed by Dallas with 13,072, Baltimore with 11,724, Las Vegas with 8,860 and Atlanta with 8,753.All five of the top millennial destinations had median home-sale prices below $450,000, Forbes reported.“Gen Zers are chasing opportunity, while millennials are chasing space,” Redfin principal economist Sheharyar Bokhari said.He said younger adults were choosing cities where they could establish careers and social lives, while millennials were more focused on locations where incomes could stretch further and homeownership was more attainable.“But young Americans aren’t fleeing expensive cities for the cheapest place they can find: Most are making relatively short moves, suggesting they want a better job or lower cost of living without giving up their existing networks,” Bokhari said, according to the New York Post.Shorter moves gain importanceThe Redfin analysis also showed that young Americans are becoming less likely to move outside their existing metropolitan areas.About 14% of 19-to-24-year-olds moved outside their metro area in 2024, down from 15% in 2014.The analysis used the Census Bureau's 2024 American Community Survey. It defined adult Gen Zers as people aged 19 to 27 and millennials as those aged 28 to 43.The data points to differences in the destinations chosen by the two generations. Gen Z's leading destinations included San Antonio, Austin, Washington, DC and Nashville, while millennials favoured Houston, Dallas, Baltimore, Las Vegas and Atlanta.Housing costs remain a notable difference between the major cities losing residents and some of the destinations gaining them.San Antonio's median home-sale price was $264,825, compared with $832,000 in New York, according to Forbes.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.body: Indian-origin Congressman Ro Khanna took a potshot at Indian-origin MAGA commentator Dinesh D'Souza after D'Souza defended his daughter, Danielle D'Souza, the wife of Rep Brandon Gill, as an American because she is a Christian born in America to a white mother. The defense was necessitated by Hasan Piker's attack on Brandon Gill that his wife is Indian -- but the qualifiers that Dinesh D'Souza used to prove that his daughter is an American came under criticism.Democrat leader Ro Khanna said: "Dinesh, like your daughter I was born in America & have an Indian immigrant father. I am Hindu and my mom is not white. Does that make me any less American or matter in any sense?"Citing Abraham Lincoln's July 4 speech from 1858, Ro Khanna said Lincoln solved this conundrum as to who can be considered an American long ago. "Lincoln said that if you believe in the Constitution, if you believe in the Declaration of Independence, then there is an electric chord that links your heart to the hearts of the men who fought in the Revolution for those principles, and that you are blood of the blood and flesh of the flesh of our founders. He articulated why our nation, unique in the history of the world, is constituted based on a devotion to a common set of ideals and principles," Khanna wrote."Dinesh the irony is that the President you worked for --Ronald Reagan --who gave an Indian immigrant with a thick accent a job in his White House knew this Lincoln passage very well," Khanna added.How did the controversy start?Streamer Hasan Piker told Axios that America conducts more terrorism than Al-Qaeda. Republican leader Brandon Gill said Piker is a living example why US should end birthright citizenship -- as Piker was born in America to Turkish nationals. "My wife is an American, born in America to American citizens. She deeply loves our nation and its culture. articles.title: Millions urged to evacuate as Typhoon Dujuan hits Japan
articles.summary: The country's meteorological agency had warned of an "imminent threat to life," but this has now been downgraded in most areas.
articles.body:
Almost two million people are under evacuation orders in Japan as Typhoon Dujuan batters a number of the country's prefectures.

Japan's Meteorological Agency had warned of an "imminent threat to life", but several warnings have now been downgraded, with the danger to life warning remaining in place in Oshima Town.

Strong winds caused power cuts for more than 50,000 people, while hundreds of flights have been cancelled and rail services have been suspended.

Dujuan has had sustained winds of 130km/h (80.8mph) and gusts of 194 km/h. It is the latest in a series of storms in the Pacific, made more intense by the "super El Niño", which has warmed the ocean, fuelling the formation of storms.

The level three warnings, for heavy rain, and the level four warnings, for landslides have now been either downgraded or lifted by the Japan Meteorological Agency in most areas.

The level four warnings remain in Shinagawa Ward, Toshima Village, and Niijima Village.

Authorities have advised the public to pay attention to weather information.

Dujuan, which is Japan's 25th typhoon of the year, has hit in the midst of a five-day holiday and forced the cancellation of several events.

Concerts scheduled for Monday at the Rock in Japan music festival have been cancelled, while the Tokyo Game Show, a video game convention, has also cancelled Monday's programme.

Japan's Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi has reportedly delayed her trip to the United States this week to monitor the effects of the typhoon.

She had been due in New York on Tuesday to meet with US President Donald Trump and speak at the UN General Assembly.

The Yokosuka City Fire Department told the BBC that a woman who lived in the house, aged in her 60s, may have been swept away and is believed to have been buried alive.

Separately, Sodegaura City Fire Department in Chiba prefecture told the BBC a man in his 50s was rescued after getting trapped while working to clear debris at a landslide site.

The department said the worker fell into a bamboo thicket, along with some heavy machinery. He was then taken to hospital.

Firefighters in Kanagawa prefecture said they received a call from a man who reported his house had been crushed by a landslide.

Some research suggests that Japan has become more exposed to destructive storms, but climate change is not thought to be increasing the number of these storms globally, and could even make them less common in some regions.

As temperatures rise, typhoons that do form are likely to become more intense on average, however.

Warmer ocean waters mean storms can pick up more energy, leading to higher wind speeds.

And because a warmer atmosphere can hold more moisture, these storms could also bring heavier rainfall.

This year, El Niño - the natural weather phenomenon bringing warmer water to parts of the tropical Pacific - is another factor.

El Niño doesn't have a clear effect on the total number of typhoons, but it can affect where typhoons form, their strength and which countries they hit.

Some El Niño events may expose Japan to stronger typhoons, for example.

The typhoon is continuing to travel along the country's Pacific coast, heading north. The extent of the damage today may not be known until Tuesday.

Additional reporting by Chie Kobayashi and Mark Poynting, climate reporter

articles.title: Sheffield's climate bond scheme funding school solar panels
articles.summary: Sheffield City Council is renewing a climate bond after the first £1m funded school solar panels.
articles.body:
Money raised by a climate investment scheme will see solar panels installed in schools to boost renewable energy and reduce energy costs.

The scheme was funded by the first phase of the Sheffield Climate Investment bond, which has raised £1m so far.

Sheffield City Council said it would issue a second climate bond initiative later in 2026, with ambitions to fund further solar panels as well as other projects.

"We have plans to move forward with more schemes which will generate energy and money for schools, communities and the council going forward," said councillor Alexi Dimond, chair of the transport, regeneration and climate policy committee.

The climate bond, launched through a specialist investment firm in December 2025, allowed residents to spend a minimum of £5 to fund climate-related council projects.

Bond buyers gained a return on their five-year investment plus their money back, the authority said.

A recent meeting of the council's transport, regeneration and climate policy agreed to commission a 25-year contract to operate and maintain solar panels on the roofs of 21 city schools, the Local Democracy Reporting Service said.

The electricity generated will be used by schools and the excess can be sold to the national grid.

"Solar panels on schools is a clear win-win," said Minesh Parekh, Crookes and Crosspool councillor and Labour's climate lead.

"Schools generating solar power helps us with our ambitions to reach net zero, but it also cuts their energy bills so that our schools can spend more on pupils' learning experiences."

articles.title: Yemenis flee across Red Sea as Houthis and Saudi-backed forces escalate war
articles.summary: The BBC's Frank Gardner speaks to some of those who have fled the war by crossing the Red Sea to Djibouti.
articles.body:
Ibrahim Issa, 50, is from the Yemeni coastal town of Dhubab, right on the front lines of the war between Yemen's Houthis and the Saudi-backed pro-government forces fighting them.

Today he sits, surrounded by his family, on a tarpaulin spread over a sandy floor inside a vast open-sided warehouse at Markazi camp in Obock, northern Djibouti, packed with Yemeni families who have fled by boat across the narrow Bab al-Mandab Strait.

After their sea crossing, Yemeni refugees have made their way by truck and on foot to this camp, jointly administered by the government and the UN.

"How could I just sit there when my kids are screaming and shaking in terror?" says Ibrahim Issa. "When the sound of the planes start, and the kids hear the planes, they begin shouting and screaming. As parents it is our responsibility, what can you do when you see this? That is why we fled, to save them."

Saudi Arabia issues first air raid alerts for Riyadh since Houthis escalated attacks

Lightning Houthi advance in Yemen may bring dangerous new dimension to Iran war

As a fisherman, Ibrahim Issa already owned a boat large enough to bring out his family from Yemen.

He even brought several of the family's goats which I can now see nibbling at scraps nearby, foraging amidst the discarded canisters of cooking gas and empty plastic bottles. Some families have been able to bring small bundles of possessions with them from Yemen – one family has even brought a "jeraak", a tall metal shisha pipe – but others have arrived, exhausted, in just the clothes they left in.

In just the last few days more than 3,000 refugees have arrived here from Yemen, many entire families. The UN estimates that in all, more than 120,000 Yemenis have been displaced by the sudden surge in fighting along Yemen's Red Sea coast.

This month, the country's Houthis, who had already seized most of the populated parts of Yemen years ago, made a lightning dash down the coast towards Bab al-Mandab, the narrow, maritime chokepoint where the southern Red Sea flows into the Gulf of Aden and the wider Indian Ocean.

Saudi Arabia, which backs the internationally recognised government of Yemen, has responded with hundreds of air strikes along the flat, coastal plain where the Houthis are now digging in. The Houthis have also launched hundreds of drones and missiles at cities and infrastructure in south-western Saudi Arabia.

"We don't care which side it is that's attacking," is the message I got loud and clear in Arabic from everyone here I spoke to. "It's the bombs falling all around us that have caused us to flee."

Djibouti, a tiny former French colony that sits just across the water from Yemen, has made it clear it has no intention of involving itself in the war between the Houthis and the Saudi-backed Yemeni government.

And yet Djibouti is one of the most militarised nations in Africa. Since 2003, the US has run a huge multinational base here, Camp Lemonnier, once home to the French Foreign Legion. China too has a major base here, its largest military presence on the Indian Ocean and recently upgraded.

Back in Markazi camp, one of those I spoke to is Qassim Abraham Abssy. Once also a fisherman, his identity card shows him to be 100 years old.

"What led us to come here?" he asks rhetorically.

"It was the planes. The sounds of the planes, boom! That's what made us flee, for the sake of our children. It burns ours hearts. We don't know which side they are from. They are bombing everywhere, because the Houthis are everywhere, in the mountains, in the roads. A plane comes, bombs everywhere."

Outside in the blazing 37C heat, close to the neat lines of tents supplied by the UN refugee agency, UNHCR, I met Mohammed Abdullarim from Aden, a 63-year-old former tour guide old enough to have been born when Aden was still a British protectorate.

Unlike the new arrivals, Mohammed has been here since 2015. He fled to Djibouti soon after the fighting first flared up between the Houthis and the government of the now-ousted President Abdrabbuh Mansour Hadi.

He has been at the camp ever since but suddenly, as we were talking, the sadness of what is happening to his country overwhelmed him and he turned his head away, choking back tears.

"Most of the people here are in the worst condition, inside the tents here. I am very touched, I'm crying for these people, for my people, for their suffering. I want our voices to be heard by the NGOs and the Djibouti government. And I'm thankful to them for accepting us."

How long will they have to stay here? That depends, of course, on the fighting. Yemen has been wracked by a horrific civil war that has killed tens of thousands of people and displaced millions since 2014.

A shaky, UN-brokered 2022 truce between the Saudis and the Houthis has broken down spectacularly in recent months, with the two sides trading missiles, drones and air strikes.

Yemen's war may be a remote one to most people but the effect of choking off Saudi Arabia's oil exports through the Bab al-Mandab Strait are well publicised. But as ever, it is often the human cost that goes unnoticed.

Sitting beside his wife on their tarpaulin, amid the cacophony all around them, Qassim Abssy the fisherman is wary of leaving the safety of Djibouti: "If the war continues then we're not going back because we have peace here."

His wife, Aisha Abdulkadir Mohammed, agrees. "We are willing to go back in peace if peace returns to our country, and we are praying to God that peace does return. All we need is peace, even for our children's future, they get safety first, then food, water and an education.

"As you see we just fled with our clothes, and left everything behind, because [in Yemen] there is no peace."

articles.title: Howdy, Hanuman! In Texas, Statue of Union meets politics of division
articles.summary: US News: TOI correspondent from Washington: Everything is supposed to be bigger in Texas, a state where cats are the size of dogs, dogs are the size of Europea.
articles.body: TOI correspondent from Washington: Everything is supposed to be bigger in Texas, a state where cats are the size of dogs, dogs are the size of European cars, where you can fit two Germanys and 20 Belgiums – or 158 of the world’s smaller countries – into it.But apparently, Texas’s Christian conservatives are not capacious enough to accommodate a large – very large – statue of Hanuman.Amid an uprush of "Hanumania" in India following a Hanuman Ansh movie documenting the life of the mystic Neem Karoli Baba, the largest state in contiguous America has been witnessing a blazing row over a 90-foot Hanuman statue towering over the Sri Ashtalakshmi Temple in Sugar Land outside Houston.Conceived as a monument to strength, devotion, and unity by local Hindu groups, and officially called the Statue of the Union, the icon has become an unlikely lightning rod in Texas’ increasingly heated argument over immigration, religion, identity and what counts as “American.”The 90-foot, 90-ton figure was officially unveiled in August 2024 after a three-day consecration ceremony and is counted as the fourth-tallest statue in the US, behind the Birth of the New World, the Statue of Liberty, and Florida’s Pegasus and Dragon.But no sooner was it installed, it attracted controversy, with members of a local church calling it a “false god” and local politicians jumping on the issue to assert that it has no place in a “Christian nation” – which, constitutionally, the US is not.Since then, arguments for and against the statue have surfaced frequently in an increasingly toxic atmosphere in a once-capacious state that has seen a large influx of Indian-origin residents, particularly in and around Dallas and Houston.Indian-American community leaders maintain that the statue is not an assertion that Texas has suddenly become India, but rather that Hindu Americans are part of Texas.“There’s nothing that’s un-American about it,” says Dr Vijay Sreenarasimhaiah, a former temple board member, arguing that the statue’s message of bringing people together reflected constitutional values.Temple members also say the structure is fully legal and they followed all due permitting processes.Engineers designed the structure to withstand hurricane-force winds exceeding 180 mph that the area is sometimes subjected to.The statue was constructed by traditional Indian sthapatis, or temple sculptors, shipped to Texas in pieces and assembled on site. The project cost about $8 million and was financed through donations from Hindus in Houston and elsewhere in the US.((The idea for the statue came from Sri Chinna Jeeyar Swami, the Indian spiritual leader who also conceived Hyderabad’s Statue of Equality. He envisioned Hanuman as a “builder of bridges” and a symbol of unity, and named it the Statue of Union because Hanuman, in the Ramayana, helps reunite Rama and Sita.))The irony is that Hanuman is hardly a recent immigrant to America. At the Mount Madonna Centre in California, the Sankat Mochan Hanuman Temple grew out of the devotion of American followers of Neem Karoli Baba, venerated by a legion of celebrities in Silicon Valley, Hollywood, and Bollywood – from the late Steve Jobs and Mark Zuckerberg to Julia Roberts and Virat Kohli.After Baba’s death in 1973, American devotees commissioned a Hanuman murti; the temple was consecrated in 2003.In New Mexico, the Neem Karoli Baba Ashram likewise traces its Hanuman devotion to American followers from the late 1970s.In Texas itself, the Karya Siddhi Hanuman temple in Frisco developed from a satsang group formed in 1999; its stone shrine was carved in Bengaluru and assembled by a team of 29 sculptors in 2015.And the cultural reach of Hanuman extends far beyond Hindu immigrants. Barack Obama, hardly the image of an Indian religious traditionalist, disclosed in a 2016 interview that among the small objects he carried in his pocket as personal reminders and good-luck charms was a miniature Hanuman figurine given to him by a woman.The National Archives confirms the existence of a Hanuman figurine in the Obama presidential collection.The backlash, however, has migrated from theology into politics amid increasing race-baiting and xenophobia in the MAGA universe. In February this year, Carlos Turcios, a Texas conservative activist, released a social-media video of the statue, describing it as evidence that “third world aliens” were taking over Texas and America.And last month, conservative commentator Kaylee Campbell pushed ahead with the fear-mongering with the question: “How is anyone supposed to take Texas seriously when we have a 90-foot ‘monkey god’ statue?”Texas politicians themselves have sent mixed signals. Governor Greg Abbott, while not specifically commenting on the statue, has publicly courted Texas’ Indian-American community, saying at a Diwali celebration, “As long as I am governor of this great state, Texas will be a land for the Indian community.” But the fireworks just won’t stop.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Taunton Brewhouse Theatre may shut in 'devastating' blow
articles.summary: A 50-year-old theatre could be forced to close in October after "prolonged" challenging conditions.
articles.body:
A town's "lifeline" theatre could be forced to close at the end of next month.

The chair of Taunton Theatre Association, a charity that runs the town's Brewhouse Theatre, said the shock announcement came with "heartfelt regret".

Val Hammond said all planned performances and activities would continue until the end of October, while the trustees tried to raise funds and find ways to cut costs. "It will be devastating for the whole town to lose such an important cultural venue," she said.

The trustees said the theatre's financial problems came after a "prolonged period of challenging trading conditions" exacerbated by this summer's heatwaves, which saw some shows cancelled.

Wayfarers Pantomime Society has performed at the Brewhouse every year that the theatre has been open since 1977.

The amateur group is currently rehearsing Aladdin, which it is due to perform there next year.

Martin Lock, chair of Wayfarers Pantomime Society, said he was told the news in a call from the theatre's executive director.

"This is absolutely devastating news for us. We are already a month into rehearsals for our January pantomime.

"We've been there right from the start, right from when it opened."

Taunton Brewhouse is owned by Somerset Council, operated by Taunton Theatre Association Ltd, a charity, and receives funding from Taunton Town Council.

The charity has overseen the theatre since 2013, following a previous closure when the theatre went into administration .

The venue, which is due to celebrate its 50th anniversary next year, was awarded £527,000 by Arts Council England in April, but that money was for an upgrade of the auditorium and studio lighting and cannot be used for day-to-day costs.

In November last year, Taunton Town Council said it would pay £105,000 a year for the next five years to the Brewhouse to secure its future and help with ongoing maintenance and repairs.

The council stepped in after Somerset Council, the building's owner, said "it was no longer financially sustainable" to continue funding the venue's repairs.
